summary: Iteration 15 — Re-verification of audit-endpoint fix from iter 14. Fix confirmed working. Ran the full 30-case audit-scoping suite (test_audit_scoping_iter14.py) against preview URL: 30/30 PASSED (100%). Both previously failing bulk-view cases (test_01_admin_bulk_200, test_02_director_bulk_200) now succeed. Direct curl also confirmed: GET /api/audit as admin → 200 with list of 176 entries; GET /api/audit as director → 200 with list of 176 entries; response shape correct (audit_id/entity/entity_id/action/user_id/user_name/user_role/details/timestamp — no ObjectId leaks). Fix RCA: server.py:2002 now wraps response through `_strip_oids(d)` helper (defined at server.py:484-492) which recursively strips `_id` keys and converts ObjectId/datetime to JSON-safe primitives — same helper already used by master_audit_list at server.py:950. One-off DB cleanup on audit_logs/master_audit_logs (unsetting nested `details.new._id`, `details.old._id`, `new_value._id`, `old_value._id`) is a belt-and-braces improvement — even without cleanup, the recursive `_strip_oids` sanitizer alone is sufficient. Regression spot-check: test_phase2_approval_chain.py + test_admin_master_module.py — 72/72 PASSED, no regressions. No other test files from Phase 1/2a/2b/2c/3a were requested and the review request explicitly permitted skipping them if the two above weren't applicable. Backend-only per request; no frontend testing performed.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:2002 — `return [_strip_oids(d) for d in logs]` correctly reuses the shared recursive sanitizer. Consistent with master_audit_list at line 950 (DRY, single source of truth for audit-serialization).

server.py:484-492 `_strip_oids` — handles ObjectId → str, datetime → isoformat, dict (drops any `_id` key at every level), list — covers all known audit_logs corruption patterns. Defence-in-depth: even if a future write inserts nested ObjectIds again, reads will not 500.

OPTIONAL (already logged in iter 14 action_items #2) — the `audit()` helper writer could also sanitize `details.old`/`details.new` at insert time to prevent future bad rows. Not blocking; current read-side fix is sufficient.
